text:
Asha: pushed a few comps for the rollout list — compact rows with an inline canary toggle. link: https://figma.redwood/rollout/compact-toggle-v1 Asha: main goal: reduce vertical noise in the history timeline and surface the toggle so PMs can flip small experiments quickly. Riley: visually it's cleaner, but a couple accessibility flags: focus order, screen reader labels, and the percent badge needs text alternatives. Noah: agree re: SR. If the toggle is first in the DOM, NVDA will announce the control before the variant name which reads oddly. Could we keep DOM order = name then toggle, and visually float the toggle left with CSS? Priya: floating works but watch tab stop order. CSS-only reorder doesn't change TAB order — we need to ensure visual order matches reading order or add aria-flowto/aria-labelledby. Asha: ok — prefer DOM = logical order (name, percent, toggle) and use flex-row-reverse to get the visual layout. Then add aria-describedby to the toggle: "variant-123-desc" that contains the percent and a short purpose sentence. Noah: markup suggestion: ```html
Checkout A (5%) 5% traffic to Checkout A. Toggling starts a canary rollout.
``` Priya: also make the toggle accessible by keyboard with a 44px hit target and visible focus outline. Current compact CSS trims padding. Riley: copy note: "Start canary" vs "Enable variant" — product wants explicit verbs. I prefer "Start canary \u2014 Checkout A" so it's clear which variant is affected. Asha: yeah explicit copy + variant name inline is better for discovery. We'll show the full phrase in the toggle and the shorter label for tiny screens. Sam: telemetry: ensure we emit events for both intent and confirmation. Something like canary_initiated_intent and canary_confirmed with {variant_id, user_id, method:"ui"}. Also include whether undo happened. Noah: about undo: inline undo link will push layout and make rows taller. Toast undo is simpler and consistent with other flows. But users scanning the timeline might miss the toast. Could combine: toast undo + a reversible timeline entry (fast rollback action). Priya: good compromise. Toast shows Undo for 8s. Timeline entry created immediately with status "canary: starting" and a rollback action. For keyboard users, toast should be reachable via a skip link or a focusable live-region action. Asha: focus management question: after hitting toggle, does focus stay on the toggle or move to toast? I think stay on the toggle so the user can continue tabbing within the row. Provide a "View rollout details" inline link with aria-live so SR users know about the change. Riley: agree. Add aria-live="polite" region that announces "Canary started for Checkout A, 5% traffic. View details." and include a visible tiny CTA to open history. Sam: color/contrast: the percent badge uses brand-blue on white, currently 4.2:1. I'll update token to hit 4.5:1. Also flag for disabled/toggled state contrast. Noah: performance note: toggling should be optimistic UI but we need to show in-progress state (spinner in button) and avoid duplicate clicks. Add aria-busy to the row during request. Priya: testing checklist for the PR: keyboard tab order, screen reader announcement, focus trap behavior if confirmation modal is required, contrast check, telemetry events. I'll author and attach it. Asha: short actions: - Asha: update comp with DOM-preserving reorder and explicit "Start canary \u2014 Checkout A" copy (EOD) - Noah: add markup sample + keyboard gif to Figma (tomorrow) - Priya: write test checklist (48h) - Sam: update color token and confirm telemetry event names (ASAP) - Riley: validate SR announcements on NVDA/VoiceOver (next week) ux-bot: note added to ticket RW-4321: accessibility checklist required for rollout toggle. Asha: thanks all. If no blockers I'll land the comp and open a design->eng PR for implementation details. :raised_hands:
